The 2001–02 season was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 88th competitive season, 10th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]] and 96th year as a club.

==Season summary==

The 2001–02 campaign was the first full season under Italian manager [[Claudio Ranieri]], who had replaced his compatriot [[Gianluca Vialli]] after five matches of the previous season.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/925944.stm | work=BBC News | title=Ranieri's Chelsea deal | date=15 September 2000}}</ref> He made his first signing in the shape of French defender [[William Gallas]] for £6.2&nbsp;million from [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], before signing [[Frank Lampard]] from [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] for £11&nbsp;million on 14 June.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/jun/14/newsstory.sport7 | location=London | work=The Guardian | first=Sean | last=Ingle | title=Lampard signs for Chelsea | date=14 June 2001}}</ref> Lampard went on to become Chelsea's highest goal scorer of all time. The signing of Lampard allowed Chelsea to part company with their captain [[Dennis Wise]], who ended his successful 12-season spell at the club by joining [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] for £1.6&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/19/leicester_wise_ap/ | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130215183505/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/19/leicester_wise_ap/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=15 February 2013 | work=CNN | title=Wise joins Leicester soccer team}}</ref> The third and final signing of the window was of French midfielder and [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] winner [[Emmanuel Petit]], who joined from [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] for £7.5&nbsp;million on 26 June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/chelsea-clinch-75m-petit-deal-6355098.html|title=Chelsea clinch £7.5m Petit deal|date=13 April 2012}}</ref>

Chelsea players encountered controversy in the second round of the UEFA Cup, when they were due to face [[Hapoel Tel Aviv F.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] on 18 October 2001. Six Chelsea first-team players—[[Albert Ferrer]], [[William Gallas]], [[Emmanuel Petit]], [[Graeme Le Saux]], [[Eiður Guðjohnsen]] and captain [[Marcel Desailly]]—did not fly to [[Israel]] due to fears since the [[September 11 attacks]] in the previous month and recent Palestinian insurgency. Chelsea lost the match 2–0, with Desailly's replacement, the Ugandan teenager [[Joel Kitamirike]], making mistakes in his only match for Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/uefa_cup/1605181.stm | work=BBC News | title=Hapoel stun subdued Chelsea | date=18 October 2001}}</ref> The six players returned for the second leg at Stamford Bridge, but a 1–1 draw saw Chelsea eliminated by an underdog for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/nov/02/uefa.sport2 | location=London | work=The Guardian | first=Jon | last=Brodkin | title=Hapoel leave Chelsea with the blues | date=1 November 2001}}</ref>

The club came sixth in the Premier League, as they had done the previous season, and reached their third FA Cup final in six seasons. In [[2002 FA Cup Final|the final]] against London rivals and Premier League champions [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]] on 4 May 2002, Chelsea lost 2–0 with both goals in the last twenty minutes of the match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/Competitions/FACompetitions/TheFACup/History/cupfinalresults/2002chelseaarsenal|title = The website for the English football association, the Emirates FA Cup and the England football team}}</ref> Chelsea were led out into the final by [[Roberto Di Matteo]], who had announced his retirement earlier in the season due to a long-term absence with a leg fracture.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McLean |first1=Max |title=5 things Chelsea can learn from their FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal in 2002 for the rematch in 2017 |url=https://www.independent.ie/world-news/and-finally/5-things-chelsea-can-learn-from-their-fa-cup-final-defeat-to-arsenal-in-2002-for-the-rematch-in-2017-35646870.html |access-date=15 October 2020 |work=Irish Independent |date=23 April 2017}}</ref>

==Team kit==
The team kit was produced by [[Umbro]] and the shirt sponsor was the airline [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] and bore the "Fly Emirates" logo. Chelsea's home kit was all blue with a white trimmed collar. Their new away kit was all white with blue socks. The club's third kit for this season was orange with blue shorts and accents.
